"""studio-svc configuration.

The shared envelope (bind addresses, Postgres, NATS, OIDC, OTLP, audit HMAC
keys) comes from ``omnicore_svc_runtime.config.load_base("STUDIO")``, which
also derives:

- ``service_name`` -> ``"studio-svc"``
- ``oidc_allowed_azp`` -> ``("studio-bff", "shell-bff", "studio-svc-worker")``
  unless ``STUDIO_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` overrides it.

Story #965 (Voice Profiles) added Studio's first AI surface: the LITELLM_*
fields back VoiceService. The AI_DEV_MODE / AI_TEST_MODE flags are the
unified, repo-wide backend-mode selectors from
omnicore_svc_runtime.ai.resolve_llm_backend_mode — not per-service vars.

Studio adds its own AI/TTS/files-client fields:

- LLM / AI (Story #965 — Studio's first AI surface: VoiceService). Mirrors
  range-svc naming. All optional: a stack without AI config still boots;
  VoiceService aborts UNAVAILABLE when no client is wired.
- Propaganda Analysis vision model (Epic #1090 / stories #1096-#1097). Image
  material routes here via the ollama_chat/ provider (vLLM strips multimodal
  image content — see platform/compose/config/litellm.yaml); text material
  (SCAME/MARCO) stays on ``litellm_gen_model``. Read by the studio-svc-worker's
  AnalyzePropagandaConsumer.
- Text to Speech (Epic #1064, sub-issues #1065-#1070). The legacy MediaServer
  microservice — which already implements Kokoro, Qwen3-TTS voice cloning, and
  VibeVoice behind one unified endpoint — is reused directly. Defaults to
  legacy's own localhost dev address so a stack/unit-test run with the var
  unset never reaches a real network address. Read by
  studio_svc.tts.client.TTSClient (studio-svc-worker only).
- Files-svc raw-file lookup (worker-side only): resolving a voice sample's
  reference WAV bytes for Qwen3-TTS voice cloning requires a real
  cross-service gRPC call to files-svc's DocumentService.GetRawFile — the ONLY
  inter-Python-service call this service makes. Empty ``files_svc_addr`` OR
  empty ``studio_svc_worker_client_secret`` disables the client entirely (no
  network attempt); the worker then fails that job with a clear, user-safe
  error_reason rather than crashing. See
  studio_svc.files.client.FilesRawFileClient and studio_svc.files.token.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from typing import Final

from omnicore_svc_runtime.config import (
    BaseServiceConfig,
    ConfigError,
    bool_env,
    int_env,
    load_base,
    optional_env,
)

# ConfigError is re-exported so callers (main.py, worker.py) catch it off this
# module rather than reaching into the runtime for the one exception studio-svc's
# own load() raises.
__all__ = ["ENV_PREFIX", "GOOSE_TABLE", "SCHEMA", "Config", "ConfigError", "load"]

ENV_PREFIX: Final = "STUDIO"
SCHEMA: Final = "studio"
GOOSE_TABLE: Final = "goose_db_version_studio"

_DEFAULT_STUDIO_VISION_MODEL: Final = "lukey03/qwen3.5-9b-abliterated-vision"
_DEFAULT_MEDIASERVER_URL: Final = "http://localhost:9003"
_DEFAULT_WORKER_CLIENT_ID: Final = "studio-svc-worker"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Config(BaseServiceConfig):
    """Immutable studio-svc configuration. Construct via :func:`load`."""

    # LLM / AI (Story #965 — Studio's first AI surface: VoiceService).
    # Unified backend-mode flags (omnicore_svc_runtime.ai) — all optional: a
    # stack without AI config still boots; VoiceService aborts UNAVAILABLE
    # when no client is wired.
    ai_dev_mode: bool = False  # AI_DEV_MODE=true → local Ollama via litellm
    ai_test_mode: bool = False  # AI_TEST_MODE=true → StubLLM (wins over ai_dev_mode)
    litellm_url: str = ""
    litellm_gen_model: str = ""
    litellm_api_key: str = ""  # NEVER logged
    # Client-side READ timeout in seconds for LiteLLM calls (Task 2, ticket
    # #2686 Stage 0 — "client-side fail-fast"). Was a hardcoded 180s; a
    # Tailscale black-hole (connect succeeds, no response) hung a worker for
    # 3 minutes with nothing but a spinner. Short default so an unreachable
    # backend fails in low tens of seconds.
    litellm_timeout_s: int = 20

    # Propaganda Analysis vision model (Epic #1090 / stories #1096-#1097).
    # Image material routes here via the ollama_chat/ provider (vLLM strips
    # multimodal image content — see platform/compose/config/litellm.yaml);
    # text material (SCAME/MARCO) stays on litellm_gen_model above. Read by
    # the studio-svc-worker's AnalyzePropagandaConsumer.
    studio_vision_model: str = _DEFAULT_STUDIO_VISION_MODEL

    # Text to Speech (Epic #1064, sub-issues #1065-#1070). The legacy
    # MediaServer microservice — which already implements Kokoro, Qwen3-TTS
    # voice cloning, and VibeVoice behind one unified endpoint — is reused
    # directly rather than building new model-serving infra. Same env-var
    # name/convention as legacy; defaults to legacy's own localhost dev
    # address so a stack/unit-test run with the var unset never reaches a
    # real network address. Read by studio_svc.tts.client.TTSClient
    # (studio-svc-worker only — the gRPC handler never calls the MediaServer).
    mediaserver_url: str = _DEFAULT_MEDIASERVER_URL

    # Files-svc raw-file lookup (worker-side only): resolving a voice
    # sample's reference WAV bytes for Qwen3-TTS voice cloning requires a
    # real cross-service gRPC call to files-svc's
    # DocumentService.GetRawFile — the ONLY inter-Python-service call this
    # service makes. Empty ``files_svc_addr`` OR empty
    # ``studio_svc_worker_client_secret`` disables the client entirely (no
    # network attempt); the worker then fails that job with a clear,
    # user-safe error_reason rather than crashing. See
    # studio_svc.files.client.FilesRawFileClient and studio_svc.files.token.
    #
    # Gate 2 is now wired on both ends: the studio-svc-worker Keycloak client
    # carries an aud=files-svc mapper alongside its aud=studio-svc one, and
    # files-svc's FILES_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP includes "studio-svc-worker". What
    # remains is DEPLOYMENT env: platform/compose/studio-svc-worker.yml must
    # set FILES_SVC_ADDR (files-svc:50051) and
    # STUDIO_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET (from
    # OIDC_STUDIO_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET) or the client stays disabled.
    files_svc_addr: str = ""
    studio_svc_worker_client_id: str = _DEFAULT_WORKER_CLIENT_ID
    studio_svc_worker_client_secret: str = ""  # NEVER logged


def load() -> Config:
    """Load Config from process env. Raises ConfigError on bad config."""
    base = load_base(ENV_PREFIX)
    return Config(
        **{f.name: getattr(base, f.name) for f in fields(base)},
        ai_dev_mode=bool_env("AI_DEV_MODE", False),
        ai_test_mode=bool_env("AI_TEST_MODE", False),
        litellm_url=optional_env("LITELLM_URL"),
        litellm_gen_model=optional_env("LITELLM_GEN_MODEL"),
        litellm_api_key=optional_env("LITELLM_API_KEY"),
        litellm_timeout_s=int_env("LITELLM_TIMEOUT_S", 20),
        studio_vision_model=optional_env("STUDIO_VISION_MODEL", _DEFAULT_STUDIO_VISION_MODEL),
        mediaserver_url=optional_env("MEDIASERVER_URL", _DEFAULT_MEDIASERVER_URL),
        files_svc_addr=optional_env("FILES_SVC_ADDR"),
        studio_svc_worker_client_id=optional_env(
            "STUDIO_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_ID", _DEFAULT_WORKER_CLIENT_ID
        ),
        studio_svc_worker_client_secret=optional_env("STUDIO_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    )

"""Shared defensive-JSON-recovery helper for LLM-produced structured output.

Code-review fix (#1090 propaganda-analysis follow-up, Fix #7). LLMs frequently
wrap their JSON in markdown code fences, prefix it with conversational prose,
or emit a ``<think>...</think>`` reasoning block before the answer (reasoning
models such as ``qwen3.5``). :func:`recover_json` recovers the JSON object from
these common shapes — clean JSON, ```json-fenced, bare-fenced,
prose-then-fenced, and a bare (unfenced) object embedded in prose or a
reasoning block — and calls the caller-supplied ``error_factory`` (raising the
returned exception) when no JSON object can be recovered, INCLUDING when the
recovered value is valid JSON but not an object (e.g. a bare array).

Extracted out of three byte-identical implementations that differed only in
the exception type/messages they raised: ``studio_svc.propaganda.parse``,
``studio_svc.brandprofile.parse``, ``studio_svc.audienceprofile.parse``. Each
tool keeps its own domain-specific exception class and message text by
passing them in — this module owns ONLY the parsing/recovery mechanics, never
the domain error vocabulary.

Deliberately a dependency-free top-level module (mirrors the flat
``rate_limit.py``/``config.py``/``worker.py`` modules), NOT nested under
``studio_svc.llm`` — ``studio_svc.llm``'s package ``__init__`` eagerly
imports ``StubLLM`` -> ``describe_image`` -> ``workers.propaganda`` ->
``propaganda.parse``, so importing this helper as ``studio_svc.llm.*`` from
inside ``propaganda.parse`` (or either of its two siblings) would import the
``studio_svc.llm`` package first and close a circular-import loop back into
the very module doing the importing. Living outside ``studio_svc.llm``
avoids that entirely: this module imports nothing from the rest of
``studio_svc``.

This is a pure function — no DB, no I/O.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator

# Captures the body of the first markdown code fence, optionally tagged with a
# language (e.g. ```json). DOTALL so the body may span newlines.
_FENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\s*\n?(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)

# Reasoning-model scratchpad. Stripped up front so brace-like text inside the
# model's chain-of-thought can't hijack the bare-object recovery below. DOTALL
# (spans newlines) + IGNORECASE (tolerate <Think>/<THINK>).
_THINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r"<think>.*?</think>", re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)


def _try_load(candidate: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Return the parsed dict for *candidate*, or None if it is not a JSON object."""
    candidate = candidate.strip()
    if not candidate:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(candidate)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None


def _iter_balanced_objects(text: str) -> Iterator[str]:
    """Yield each top-level balanced ``{...}`` region in *text*, left to right.

    Tracks brace depth while respecting JSON string literals (and their
    backslash escapes) so braces inside string values never skew the count.
    Braces that never close are ignored. This recovers a bare JSON object even
    when it is surrounded by prose or contains nested objects.
    """
    depth = 0
    start = -1
    in_str = False
    escaped = False
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if in_str:
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif ch == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif ch == '"':
                in_str = False
            continue
        if ch == '"':
            in_str = True
        elif ch == "{":
            if depth == 0:
                start = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == "}" and depth > 0:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0 and start != -1:
                yield text[start : i + 1]
                start = -1


def _recover(text: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Try every recovery strategy against *text*; return the first object found."""
    # 1. Clean JSON (possibly surrounded by whitespace).
    parsed = _try_load(text)
    if parsed is not None:
        return parsed

    # 2. JSON inside a markdown code fence (```json ... ``` or bare ``` ... ```),
    #    tolerating any leading prose before the fence.
    for match in _FENCE_PATTERN.finditer(text):
        parsed = _try_load(match.group(1))
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    # 3. Bare (unfenced) JSON object embedded in prose — scan for the first
    #    balanced {...} region that parses as an object.
    for candidate in _iter_balanced_objects(text):
        parsed = _try_load(candidate)
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    return None


def recover_json(
    raw: str,
    *,
    error_factory: Callable[[str], Exception],
    empty_message: str,
    unparseable_message: str,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Parse an LLM response into a JSON object dict.

    Tolerates clean JSON (with surrounding whitespace), ```json / bare ```
    fenced blocks, leading conversational prose before the object, a trailing
    sign-off after it, a ``<think>...</think>`` reasoning prefix, and a bare
    (unfenced) object embedded in prose. Raises ``error_factory(empty_message)``
    on empty/blank input, and ``error_factory(unparseable_message)`` when no
    JSON object can be recovered — including when the recovered value is valid
    JSON but not a dict (e.g. a bare JSON array).

    ``error_factory`` is called with a single message string and must return
    an ``Exception`` instance to raise; passing an ``Exception`` subclass
    directly (e.g. ``error_factory=MyParseError``) works since the class
    itself is callable with that signature.
    """
    if not raw or not raw.strip():
        raise error_factory(empty_message)

    # Strip reasoning-model <think>...</think> blocks first (a no-op when absent),
    # then fall back to the raw text so a response whose ONLY object lives inside
    # a think block is still recoverable.
    cleaned = _THINK_PATTERN.sub("", raw)
    for text in (cleaned, raw) if cleaned != raw else (cleaned,):
        parsed = _recover(text)
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    raise error_factory(unparseable_message)

"""studio-svc orchestrator + graceful shutdown (boot skeleton).

Wiring sequence (mirrors services/clio-svc/src/clio_svc/main.py):

    load config
      -> bootstrap observability (logger + tracer + meter)
      -> setup OIDC JWT verifier (aud + azp allowlist — Gate 2)
      -> connect NATS
      -> run startup migrations (goose) + rotate DB role passwords
      -> create asyncpg pool
      -> spawn outbox drainer background task
      -> build gRPC server (mTLS interceptor + health + reflection)
      -> register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers
      -> serve until signal
      -> graceful shutdown (stop server, close NATS, close pool, shutdown meter + tracer)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import signal
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from omnicore_svc_runtime.auth import create_verifier
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db import Pool, create_pool
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db import migrate as db_migrate
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate import RoleCredential

from studio_svc import config as cfg_mod
from studio_svc.audit import parse_keys
from studio_svc.events import Outbox
from studio_svc.events import connect as nats_connect
from studio_svc.llm import make_llm_client
from studio_svc.observability import (
    configure_logger,
    get_logger,
    setup_meter,
    setup_tracer,
    shutdown_meter,
    shutdown_tracer,
)
from studio_svc.server import build


def _migrations_dir() -> Path:
    """Locate the migrations dir relative to the package install root.

    In the container: ``/app/migrations`` (Dockerfile COPY target).
    Outside (dev / tests): two levels up from this file
    (``src/studio_svc/main.py`` -> ``services/studio-svc/migrations``).
    Mirrors clio-svc.
    """
    container = Path("/app/migrations")
    if container.exists():
        return container
    here = Path(__file__).resolve()
    return here.parent.parent.parent / "migrations"


async def _serve(c: cfg_mod.Config) -> int:
    """Bring up every long-lived dependency and serve until SIGINT/SIGTERM."""
    log = get_logger("main")

    setup_tracer(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("tracer ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    setup_meter(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("meter ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    verifier = await create_verifier(
        issuer_url=c.oidc_issuer_url,
        internal_url=c.oidc_internal_url,
        audience=c.oidc_audience,
        allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp,
    )
    log.info("oidc verifier ready", audience=c.oidc_audience, allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp)

    publisher = await nats_connect(
        nats_url=c.nats_url, creds_file=c.nats_creds_file, ca_file=c.nats_ca_file
    )
    log.info("nats connected", url=c.nats_url)

    # Startup migrations (goose) + per-role LOGIN provisioning, BEFORE the app
    # pool opens — studio_app / studio_migrate / studio_drainer are created NOLOGIN
    # by migration 00001, so the pool can only authenticate once `up` has rotated
    # their passwords. Empty admin DSN → skipped (mirrors clio-svc).
    await db_migrate.up(
        admin_dsn=c.postgres_admin_dsn,
        migrations_dir=_migrations_dir(),
        goose_table=cfg_mod.GOOSE_TABLE,
        service="studio-svc",
        roles=(
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_app", password=c.app_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_migrate", password=c.migrate_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_drainer", password=c.drainer_db_password),
        ),
    )
    log.info("startup migrations complete")

    pool: Pool = await create_pool(
        dsn=c.postgres_dsn,
        migrator_dsn=c.postgres_migrator_dsn,
        drainer_dsn=c.postgres_drainer_dsn,
        max_size=c.postgres_max_conns,
        min_size=c.postgres_min_conns,
        max_inactive_connection_lifetime=c.postgres_max_conn_idle_time_s,
    )
    log.info(
        "postgres pool ready",
        migrator=pool.migrator is not None,
        drainer=pool.drainer is not None,
    )

    # Transactional outbox drainer. Runs in the server process, mirroring
    # clio-svc: domain handlers write studio.event_outbox rows in their own tx;
    # this background loop forwards them to NATS with Nats-Msg-Id dedup.
    # The studio-svc-worker runs its own ten AI-generation JetStream consumers
    # in a separate process (see studio_svc.worker's module docstring) — this
    # drainer is a publisher, not a consumer, and lives here regardless.
    background: list[asyncio.Task[None]] = []
    outbox = Outbox(pool=pool, publisher=publisher, schema=cfg_mod.SCHEMA)
    background.append(asyncio.create_task(outbox.run(), name="outbox"))

    audit_keys = parse_keys(c.audit_hmac_keys, active_id=c.audit_hmac_active_key_id)
    log.info("audit key provider ready", active_key_id=c.audit_hmac_active_key_id)

    # LLM client for VoiceService (Story #965 — Studio's first AI surface).
    # StubLLM in dev mode; LiteLLMClient otherwise. The API key never reaches
    # a log line.
    llm = make_llm_client(c)
    log.info(
        "llm client ready",
        dev_mode=c.ai_dev_mode,
        model=c.litellm_gen_model or "(unset)",
    )

    server = build(
        c,
        verifier=verifier,
        pool=pool,
        audit_keys=audit_keys,
        llm=llm,
    )
    await server.grpc_server.start()
    log.info("server listening", grpc=c.grpc_addr, healthz=c.healthz_addr)

    stop_event = asyncio.Event()
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    def _signal_handler() -> None:
        log.info("shutdown signal received")
        stop_event.set()

    for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
        loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _signal_handler)

    try:
        await stop_event.wait()
    finally:
        log.info("graceful shutdown begin")
        for t in background:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*background, return_exceptions=True)
        await server.stop(grace_s=10.0)
        await publisher.close()
        if llm is not None:
            await llm.close()
        await pool.close()
        shutdown_meter()
        shutdown_tracer()
        log.info("graceful shutdown complete")

    return 0


def main() -> int:
    """Process entrypoint. Returns the desired exit code."""
    configure_logger(level="INFO")
    log = get_logger("main")
    try:
        c = cfg_mod.load()
    except cfg_mod.ConfigError as exc:
        log.error("config load failed", err=str(exc))
        return 1
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_serve(c))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Per-org LiteLLM token-bucket rate limiter backed by studio.ai_rate_bucket.

The shared Studio AI rate surface (migration 00003_voice_ai_rate_bucket.sql,
introduced by the Voice Profiles epic) is a ``(org_id, bucket_key)``-keyed token
bucket plus the ``studio.consume_ai_rate_token(org, bucket_key, capacity,
refill_per_minute)`` plpgsql function — the same shape range-svc uses. Each
Studio AI surface consumes it under its own ``bucket_key`` (VoiceService uses
``voice_draft``; the brand-profile worker uses ``brand_profile``), so the
surfaces get independent per-org limits from one shared table + function.

The bucket is a classic token bucket:
  - capacity            — max tokens the bucket can hold (set on genesis).
  - refill_per_minute   — tokens added per minute, prorated to the elapsed time
    since the bucket's ``last_refill``.

Each ``consume`` runs inside ``pool.with_org(org_id)`` (RLS GUC set) and calls
the atomic consume + lazy-refill function in one round-trip. Because the whole
thing is one statement inside the caller's tx, two worker replicas serialize on
the row lock ``consume_ai_rate_token`` takes (FOR UPDATE) and share the same
per-org limit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.pool import Pool

# Phase-default: 30 generations/min per org (brand-profile generation is far
# heavier than a recipe action, so the bucket is smaller than range's 60).
DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 30
DEFAULT_REFILL_PER_MINUTE = 30

# Default bucket_key for the brand-profile worker. Other Studio AI surfaces
# (e.g. VoiceService) key the same shared table under their own bucket_key.
DEFAULT_BUCKET_KEY = "brand_profile"

# Atomic consume + lazy refill via the shared plpgsql function. Returns one row:
#   consumed BOOLEAN, retry_after_ms INT
_CONSUME_SQL = (
    "SELECT consumed, retry_after_ms "
    "FROM studio.consume_ai_rate_token($1::uuid, $2::text, $3::int, $4::int)"
)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class RateLimiter:
    """Postgres-backed per-org token-bucket rate limiter."""

    pool: Pool
    capacity: int = DEFAULT_CAPACITY
    refill_per_minute: int = DEFAULT_REFILL_PER_MINUTE
    bucket_key: str = DEFAULT_BUCKET_KEY

    async def consume(self, *, org_id: str) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        """Attempt to consume one token for ``org_id`` under ``bucket_key``.

        Returns ``(True, 0)`` when a token was available; otherwise
        ``(False, retry_after_ms)`` with the wait until the next whole token.
        """
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            row = await conn.fetchrow(
                _CONSUME_SQL,
                org_id,
                self.bucket_key,
                self.capacity,
                self.refill_per_minute,
            )
        if row is None:
            raise RuntimeError("ai_rate_bucket consume returned no row")

# Cap inbound/outbound message size for ALL RPCs. RECEIVE stays at 8 MiB — the
# smallest budget that still covers the image-upload path: an
# AnalyzePropaganda request carrying a real uploaded image's raw image_data
# bytes (MATERIAL_TYPE_IMAGE; Epic #1090, stories #1096/#1097). studio-bff caps
# the inbound HTTP request body at 8 MiB and the client caps the image itself
# at 5 MB, so 8 MiB covers the largest legitimate image payload (base64/proto
# framing overhead included) with headroom, while still bounding memory for
# every OTHER Studio RPC far tighter than a blanket cap sized for the image
# path alone would. ConvertService and ExtractionService do NOT rely on this
# transport-level cap as their sole enforcement point — they each check their
# own explicit content ceiling inside the handler (see
# convert/text_extractor.py's EXTRACT_MAX_BYTES, still 2 MiB) — so this cap
# does not widen their effective limits, only the image-upload path's.
#
# SEND is 64 MiB, deliberately larger than RECEIVE: TextToSpeech.Get returns
# synthesized audio base64-embedded in the response Struct, so response size
# scales with SCRIPT LENGTH (~4 KB/char) — a ~2.9k-character script already
# exceeds an 8 MiB cap. Every such read aborted with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, which
# studio-bff's grpcmap renders as HTTP 429, so a job that had synthesized
# perfectly well surfaced to the user as a failure. Matches the 64 MiB ceiling
# on studio-bff's CLIENT receive size (studioclient.MaxCallRecvMsgSize) — both
# sides reject independently, so they must move together.
#

#: tenant named in ``x-tenant-id`` (T9 cross-tenant adoption).
#:
#: An async worker processes jobs for EVERY org, so its ``client_credentials``
#: token cannot carry one ``org_id`` — ``x-tenant-id`` is how it hands the
#: owning org over, and without an adopt scope the interceptor rejects that
#: pair outright (F31). ``workflow-svc-worker`` needs it because the Text to
#: Speech canvas node (#1378/#1379) calls ``TextToSpeechService`` for whichever
#: org the run belongs to.
#:
#: Scoping the trust to a NAMED realm role is what keeps F31 intact: a token
#: without ``tenant:any`` still cannot name its own tenant, so a blank or
#: forged ``org_id`` claim is rejected exactly as before. The grant is an
#: auditable entry in ``platform/keycloak/realm-export.json``, not a property
#: of "being a service" — the same shape files-svc uses for the
#: studio-svc-worker -> files-svc hop.

    audit_keys: KeyProvider | None,
    llm: object | None,

    When ``pool`` is provided, ``audit_keys`` MUST also be supplied — the real
    ``PresetHandler`` + ``BrandProfileHandler`` write HMAC-chained audit rows and
    silently falling back to an embedded key would break Gate 5 (audit tamper
    detection).

    service uses its UNIMPLEMENTED fallback — existing unit tests call
    :func:`build` without a pool and must continue to pass.

    status='generating' row and enqueues a worker job; the worker (not this

        raise ValueError("audit_keys is required when pool is provided")

    tool_pb2_grpc.add_ToolServiceServicer_to_server(_UnimplementedToolHandler(), server)
    task_pb2_grpc.add_TaskServiceServicer_to_server(_UnimplementedTaskHandler(), server)

    convert_service_pb2_grpc.add_ConvertServiceServicer_to_server(ConvertHandler(), server)

        # slipped past would fail loudly rather than write an unchained audit row.

            BrandProfileHandler(pool=pool, audit_keys=audit_keys), server

consumers in total:
  - ``studio.brand_profile.generate.>`` → GenerateBrandProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.brand_profile.refine.>`` → RefineBrandProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.audience_profile.generate.>`` → GenerateAudienceProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.propaganda_analysis.analyze.>`` → AnalyzePropagandaConsumer
  - ``studio.content.generate.>`` → GenerateContentConsumer
  - ``studio.content.refine.>`` → RefineContentConsumer
  - ``studio.population_template.generate.>`` → GeneratePopulationTemplateConsumer
  - ``studio.character_generation.generate.>`` → GenerateCharactersConsumer
  - ``studio.tts.generate.>`` → GenerateTextToSpeechConsumer
  - ``studio.segmentation.generate.>`` → GenerateSegmentsConsumer
  - ``studio.content_plan.generate.>`` → GenerateContentPlanConsumer

"""Shared defensive-JSON-recovery helper for LLM-produced structured output.

Code-review fix (#1090 propaganda-analysis follow-up, Fix #7). LLMs frequently
wrap their JSON in markdown code fences, prefix it with conversational prose,
or emit a ``<think>...</think>`` reasoning block before the answer (reasoning
models such as ``qwen3.5``). :func:`recover_json` recovers the JSON object from
these common shapes — clean JSON, ```json-fenced, bare-fenced,
prose-then-fenced, and a bare (unfenced) object embedded in prose or a
reasoning block — and calls the caller-supplied ``error_factory`` (raising the
returned exception) when no JSON object can be recovered, INCLUDING when the
recovered value is valid JSON but not an object (e.g. a bare array).

Extracted out of three byte-identical implementations that differed only in
the exception type/messages they raised: ``studio_svc.propaganda.parse``,
``studio_svc.brandprofile.parse``, ``studio_svc.audienceprofile.parse``. Each
tool keeps its own domain-specific exception class and message text by
passing them in — this module owns ONLY the parsing/recovery mechanics, never
the domain error vocabulary.

Deliberately a dependency-free top-level module (mirrors the flat
``rate_limit.py``/``config.py``/``worker.py`` modules), NOT nested under
``studio_svc.llm`` — ``studio_svc.llm``'s package ``__init__`` eagerly
imports ``StubLLM`` -> ``describe_image`` -> ``workers.propaganda`` ->
``propaganda.parse``, so importing this helper as ``studio_svc.llm.*`` from
inside ``propaganda.parse`` (or either of its two siblings) would import the
``studio_svc.llm`` package first and close a circular-import loop back into
the very module doing the importing. Living outside ``studio_svc.llm``
avoids that entirely: this module imports nothing from the rest of
``studio_svc``.

This is a pure function — no DB, no I/O.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator

# Captures the body of the first markdown code fence, optionally tagged with a
# language (e.g. ```json). DOTALL so the body may span newlines.
_FENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\s*\n?(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)

# Reasoning-model scratchpad. Stripped up front so brace-like text inside the
# model's chain-of-thought can't hijack the bare-object recovery below. DOTALL
# (spans newlines) + IGNORECASE (tolerate <Think>/<THINK>).
_THINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r"<think>.*?</think>", re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)


def _try_load(candidate: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Return the parsed dict for *candidate*, or None if it is not a JSON object."""
    candidate = candidate.strip()
    if not candidate:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(candidate)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None


def _iter_balanced_objects(text: str) -> Iterator[str]:
    """Yield each top-level balanced ``{...}`` region in *text*, left to right.

    Tracks brace depth while respecting JSON string literals (and their
    backslash escapes) so braces inside string values never skew the count.
    Braces that never close are ignored. This recovers a bare JSON object even
    when it is surrounded by prose or contains nested objects.
    """
    depth = 0
    start = -1
    in_str = False
    escaped = False
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if in_str:
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif ch == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif ch == '"':
                in_str = False
            continue
        if ch == '"':
            in_str = True
        elif ch == "{":
            if depth == 0:
                start = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == "}" and depth > 0:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0 and start != -1:
                yield text[start : i + 1]
                start = -1


def _recover(text: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Try every recovery strategy against *text*; return the first object found."""
    # 1. Clean JSON (possibly surrounded by whitespace).
    parsed = _try_load(text)
    if parsed is not None:
        return parsed

    # 2. JSON inside a markdown code fence (```json ... ``` or bare ``` ... ```),
    #    tolerating any leading prose before the fence.
    for match in _FENCE_PATTERN.finditer(text):
        parsed = _try_load(match.group(1))
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    # 3. Bare (unfenced) JSON object embedded in prose — scan for the first
    #    balanced {...} region that parses as an object.
    for candidate in _iter_balanced_objects(text):
        parsed = _try_load(candidate)
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    return None


def recover_json(
    raw: str,
    *,
    error_factory: Callable[[str], Exception],
    empty_message: str,
    unparseable_message: str,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Parse an LLM response into a JSON object dict.

    Tolerates clean JSON (with surrounding whitespace), ```json / bare ```
    fenced blocks, leading conversational prose before the object, a trailing
    sign-off after it, a ``<think>...</think>`` reasoning prefix, and a bare
    (unfenced) object embedded in prose. Raises ``error_factory(empty_message)``
    on empty/blank input, and ``error_factory(unparseable_message)`` when no
    JSON object can be recovered — including when the recovered value is valid
    JSON but not a dict (e.g. a bare JSON array).

    ``error_factory`` is called with a single message string and must return
    an ``Exception`` instance to raise; passing an ``Exception`` subclass
    directly (e.g. ``error_factory=MyParseError``) works since the class
    itself is callable with that signature.
    """
    if not raw or not raw.strip():
        raise error_factory(empty_message)

    # Strip reasoning-model <think>...</think> blocks first (a no-op when absent),
    # then fall back to the raw text so a response whose ONLY object lives inside
    # a think block is still recoverable.
    cleaned = _THINK_PATTERN.sub("", raw)
    for text in (cleaned, raw) if cleaned != raw else (cleaned,):
        parsed = _recover(text)
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed

    raise error_factory(unparseable_message)

"""studio-svc orchestrator + graceful shutdown (boot skeleton).

Wiring sequence (mirrors services/clio-svc/src/clio_svc/main.py):

    load config
      -> bootstrap observability (logger + tracer + meter)
      -> setup OIDC JWT verifier (aud + azp allowlist — Gate 2)
      -> connect NATS
      -> run startup migrations (goose) + rotate DB role passwords
      -> create asyncpg pool
      -> spawn outbox drainer background task
      -> build gRPC server (mTLS interceptor + health + reflection)
      -> register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers
      -> serve until signal
      -> graceful shutdown (stop server, close NATS, close pool, shutdown meter + tracer)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import signal
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from omnicore_svc_runtime.auth import create_verifier
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db import Pool, create_pool
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db import migrate as db_migrate
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate import RoleCredential

from studio_svc import config as cfg_mod
from studio_svc.audit import parse_keys
from studio_svc.events import Outbox
from studio_svc.events import connect as nats_connect
from studio_svc.llm import make_llm_client
from studio_svc.observability import (
    configure_logger,
    get_logger,
    setup_meter,
    setup_tracer,
    shutdown_meter,
    shutdown_tracer,
)
from studio_svc.server import build


def _migrations_dir() -> Path:
    """Locate the migrations dir relative to the package install root.

    In the container: ``/app/migrations`` (Dockerfile COPY target).
    Outside (dev / tests): two levels up from this file
    (``src/studio_svc/main.py`` -> ``services/studio-svc/migrations``).
    Mirrors clio-svc.
    """
    container = Path("/app/migrations")
    if container.exists():
        return container
    here = Path(__file__).resolve()
    return here.parent.parent.parent / "migrations"


async def _serve(c: cfg_mod.Config) -> int:
    """Bring up every long-lived dependency and serve until SIGINT/SIGTERM."""
    log = get_logger("main")

    setup_tracer(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("tracer ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    setup_meter(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("meter ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    verifier = await create_verifier(
        issuer_url=c.oidc_issuer_url,
        internal_url=c.oidc_internal_url,
        audience=c.oidc_audience,
        allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp,
    )
    log.info("oidc verifier ready", audience=c.oidc_audience, allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp)

    publisher = await nats_connect(
        nats_url=c.nats_url, creds_file=c.nats_creds_file, ca_file=c.nats_ca_file
    )
    log.info("nats connected", url=c.nats_url)

    # Startup migrations (goose) + per-role LOGIN provisioning, BEFORE the app
    # pool opens — studio_app / studio_migrate / studio_drainer are created NOLOGIN
    # by migration 00001, so the pool can only authenticate once `up` has rotated
    # their passwords. Empty admin DSN → skipped (mirrors clio-svc).
    await db_migrate.up(
        admin_dsn=c.postgres_admin_dsn,
        migrations_dir=_migrations_dir(),
        goose_table=cfg_mod.GOOSE_TABLE,
        service="studio-svc",
        roles=(
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_app", password=c.app_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_migrate", password=c.migrate_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_drainer", password=c.drainer_db_password),
        ),
    )
    log.info("startup migrations complete")

    pool: Pool = await create_pool(
        dsn=c.postgres_dsn,
        migrator_dsn=c.postgres_migrator_dsn,
        drainer_dsn=c.postgres_drainer_dsn,
        max_size=c.postgres_max_conns,
        min_size=c.postgres_min_conns,
        max_inactive_connection_lifetime=c.postgres_max_conn_idle_time_s,
    )
    log.info(
        "postgres pool ready",
        migrator=pool.migrator is not None,
        drainer=pool.drainer is not None,
    )

    # clio-svc: domain handlers write studio.event_outbox rows in their own tx;
    # this background loop forwards them to NATS with Nats-Msg-Id dedup.
    # The studio-svc-worker runs its own ten AI-generation JetStream consumers
    # in a separate process (see studio_svc.worker's module docstring) — this
    # drainer is a publisher, not a consumer, and lives here regardless.
    background: list[asyncio.Task[None]] = []
    outbox = Outbox(pool=pool, publisher=publisher, schema=cfg_mod.SCHEMA)
    background.append(asyncio.create_task(outbox.run(), name="outbox"))

    audit_keys = parse_keys(c.audit_hmac_keys, active_id=c.audit_hmac_active_key_id)
    log.info("audit key provider ready", active_key_id=c.audit_hmac_active_key_id)

    # LLM client for VoiceService (Story #965 — Studio's first AI surface).
    # StubLLM in dev mode; LiteLLMClient otherwise. The API key never reaches
    # a log line.
    llm = make_llm_client(c)
    log.info(
        "llm client ready",
        dev_mode=c.ai_dev_mode,
        model=c.litellm_gen_model or "(unset)",
    )

        c,
        verifier=verifier,
        pool=pool,
        audit_keys=audit_keys,
        llm=llm,
    )
    await server.grpc_server.start()
    log.info("server listening", grpc=c.grpc_addr, healthz=c.healthz_addr)

    stop_event = asyncio.Event()
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    def _signal_handler() -> None:
        log.info("shutdown signal received")
        stop_event.set()

    for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
        loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _signal_handler)

    try:
        await stop_event.wait()
    finally:
        log.info("graceful shutdown begin")
        for t in background:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*background, return_exceptions=True)
        await server.stop(grace_s=10.0)
        await publisher.close()
        if llm is not None:
            await llm.close()
        await pool.close()
        shutdown_meter()
        shutdown_tracer()
        log.info("graceful shutdown complete")

    return 0


def main() -> int:
    """Process entrypoint. Returns the desired exit code."""
    configure_logger(level="INFO")
    log = get_logger("main")
    try:
        c = cfg_mod.load()
    except cfg_mod.ConfigError as exc:
        log.error("config load failed", err=str(exc))
        return 1
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_serve(c))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Per-org LiteLLM token-bucket rate limiter backed by studio.ai_rate_bucket.

The shared Studio AI rate surface (migration 00003_voice_ai_rate_bucket.sql,
introduced by the Voice Profiles epic) is a ``(org_id, bucket_key)``-keyed token
bucket plus the ``studio.consume_ai_rate_token(org, bucket_key, capacity,
refill_per_minute)`` plpgsql function — the same shape range-svc uses. Each
Studio AI surface consumes it under its own ``bucket_key`` (VoiceService uses
``voice_draft``; the brand-profile worker uses ``brand_profile``), so the
surfaces get independent per-org limits from one shared table + function.

The bucket is a classic token bucket:
  - capacity            — max tokens the bucket can hold (set on genesis).
  - refill_per_minute   — tokens added per minute, prorated to the elapsed time
    since the bucket's ``last_refill``.

Each ``consume`` runs inside ``pool.with_org(org_id)`` (RLS GUC set) and calls
the atomic consume + lazy-refill function in one round-trip. Because the whole
thing is one statement inside the caller's tx, two worker replicas serialize on
the row lock ``consume_ai_rate_token`` takes (FOR UPDATE) and share the same
per-org limit.

from dataclasses import dataclass

from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.pool import Pool

# Phase-default: 30 generations/min per org (brand-profile generation is far
# heavier than a recipe action, so the bucket is smaller than range's 60).

DEFAULT_REFILL_PER_MINUTE = 30

# (e.g. VoiceService) key the same shared table under their own bucket_key.

#   consumed BOOLEAN, retry_after_ms INT

                self.refill_per_minute,

# Cap inbound/outbound message size for ALL RPCs. RECEIVE stays at 8 MiB — the
# smallest budget that still covers the image-upload path: an
# AnalyzePropaganda request carrying a real uploaded image's raw image_data
# bytes (MATERIAL_TYPE_IMAGE; Epic #1090, stories #1096/#1097). studio-bff caps
# the inbound HTTP request body at 8 MiB and the client caps the image itself
# at 5 MB, so 8 MiB covers the largest legitimate image payload (base64/proto
# framing overhead included) with headroom, while still bounding memory for
# every OTHER Studio RPC far tighter than a blanket cap sized for the image
# path alone would. ConvertService and ExtractionService do NOT rely on this
# transport-level cap as their sole enforcement point — they each check their
# own explicit content ceiling inside the handler (see
# convert/text_extractor.py's EXTRACT_MAX_BYTES, still 2 MiB) — so this cap
# does not widen their effective limits, only the image-upload path's.
#
# SEND is 64 MiB, deliberately larger than RECEIVE: TextToSpeech.Get returns
# synthesized audio base64-embedded in the response Struct, so response size
# scales with SCRIPT LENGTH (~4 KB/char) — a ~2.9k-character script already
# exceeds an 8 MiB cap. Every such read aborted with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, which
# studio-bff's grpcmap renders as HTTP 429, so a job that had synthesized
# perfectly well surfaced to the user as a failure. Matches the 64 MiB ceiling
# on studio-bff's CLIENT receive size (studioclient.MaxCallRecvMsgSize) — both
# sides reject independently, so they must move together.
#

#: tenant named in ``x-tenant-id`` (T9 cross-tenant adoption).
#:
#: An async worker processes jobs for EVERY org, so its ``client_credentials``
#: token cannot carry one ``org_id`` — ``x-tenant-id`` is how it hands the
#: owning org over, and without an adopt scope the interceptor rejects that
#: pair outright (F31). ``workflow-svc-worker`` needs it because the Text to
#: Speech canvas node (#1378/#1379) calls ``TextToSpeechService`` for whichever
#: org the run belongs to.
#:

#: without ``tenant:any`` still cannot name its own tenant, so a blank or
#: forged ``org_id`` claim is rejected exactly as before. The grant is an
#: auditable entry in ``platform/keycloak/realm-export.json``, not a property
#: of "being a service" — the same shape files-svc uses for the
#: studio-svc-worker -> files-svc hop.

    audit_keys: KeyProvider | None,

    When ``pool`` is provided, ``audit_keys`` MUST also be supplied — the real
    ``PresetHandler`` + ``BrandProfileHandler`` write HMAC-chained audit rows and
    silently falling back to an embedded key would break Gate 5 (audit tamper
    detection).

    service uses its UNIMPLEMENTED fallback — existing unit tests call
    :func:`build` without a pool and must continue to pass.

    tool_pb2_grpc.add_ToolServiceServicer_to_server(_UnimplementedToolHandler(), server)
    task_pb2_grpc.add_TaskServiceServicer_to_server(_UnimplementedTaskHandler(), server)

    convert_service_pb2_grpc.add_ConvertServiceServicer_to_server(ConvertHandler(), server)

"""studio-svc-worker entrypoint — AI-generation consumers.

The worker is the second long-lived process built from the studio-svc container
image — same package, launched as ``python -m studio_svc.worker``.

It subscribes to JetStream and dispatches the AI-generation jobs — ELEVEN
consumers in total:
  - ``studio.brand_profile.generate.>`` → GenerateBrandProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.brand_profile.refine.>`` → RefineBrandProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.audience_profile.generate.>`` → GenerateAudienceProfileConsumer
  - ``studio.propaganda_analysis.analyze.>`` → AnalyzePropagandaConsumer
  - ``studio.content.generate.>`` → GenerateContentConsumer
  - ``studio.content.refine.>`` → RefineContentConsumer
  - ``studio.population_template.generate.>`` → GeneratePopulationTemplateConsumer
  - ``studio.character_generation.generate.>`` → GenerateCharactersConsumer
  - ``studio.tts.generate.>`` → GenerateTextToSpeechConsumer
  - ``studio.segmentation.generate.>`` → GenerateSegmentsConsumer
  - ``studio.content_plan.generate.>`` → GenerateContentPlanConsumer

The consumers share the same LLM client and Postgres pool but consume from
INDEPENDENT per-org rate buckets (distinct ``bucket_key`` values on the shared
``studio.ai_rate_bucket`` table), so saturating one surface's bucket never
throttles the others.

Bootstrap sequence:

    load config
      -> setup observability (logger + meter)
      -> connect NATS
      -> create asyncpg pool (app + drainer for cross-tenant bucket reads)
      -> parse audit HMAC keys (Gate 5 — the worker writes audit rows too)
      -> build LLM client (StubLLM in dev mode) + per-surface rate limiters
      -> bind /healthz HTTPServer
      -> mount each consumer as a background task, run until signal,
         graceful shutdown

If you want to:

- **Regenerate proto stubs (Go/Python/TS)**: `make proto`
- **Regenerate only TS proto stubs**: `make proto-ts`
- **Lint proto**: `make proto-lint`
- **Check proto breaking changes**: `make proto-breaking`
- **Run Go tests for a service**: `cd services/<svc> && go test -short ./...` (or `make <svc>-test`)
- **Run one Go test by name**: `go test -run '^TestName$' ./internal/...`
- **Run Go integration tests**: `go test -tags=integration -run '^TestName$' ./tests/integration/...` (or `make <svc>-test-int`, Docker required)
- **Run all Go modules + coverage file**: `make go-test` (or `make go-test-short` to skip testcontainers)
- **Check Go coverage gate**: `make go-coverage`
- **Tidy Go modules**: `make go-tidy`
- **Vet Go code**: `go vet ./...` (from service dir)
- **Run Vitest for one workspace**: `pnpm test`
- **Watch Vitest (TDD loop)**: `pnpm test:watch`
- **Run one Vitest test by name**: `pnpm test -- --run -t "<name>"`
- **Run Vitest with coverage**: `pnpm test -- --coverage`
- **Recompile Paraglide i18n messages**: `pnpm --filter @omnicore-platform/platform-chrome run compile-messages` (then hand-wire `frontends/platform-chrome/src/paraglide/messages.ts`)
- **Audit i18n locale parity/ICU/glossary**: `npx tsx scripts/i18n-audit.ts`
- **Fast glossary-only i18n check**: `cd frontends/platform-chrome && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/glossary.regression.test.ts`
- **Regenerate Range location-wizard geo shards (offline)**: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts` (network refresh: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts --fetch` first, to repopulate `scripts/geo-sources/`)
- **Lint an MFE**: `pnpm lint`
- **Typecheck an MFE**: `pnpm typecheck`
- **Bring up the whole stack (baked images)**: `make up` (`SCOPE=<vertical>` to limit, `CLEAN=1` to wipe volumes, `BUILD=1` to rebuild images from fresh proto)
- **`make up` never builds two MFE images at once — not even the ones `BUILD=` did not name**: each Vite build takes an 8GB Node heap, so the guarded loop (`_build-guarded`) builds non-MFE images in parallel and MFE images strictly one at a time. That guard used to cover only the `BUILD=`-selected set, while `up`'s final `docker compose up -d` carried no `--no-build` and every locally-built service keeps its `build:` context — so anything `BUILD=` missed and `stack-pin-images.py` could not snapshot (which is *everything* on a machine with no bare `:dev` tags left to snapshot from) was built by **compose** instead, all at once. 11 concurrent Vite builds either die with `ResourceExhausted: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build" ... cannot allocate memory` or drives an OOM-kill spiral that wedges the Docker daemon, so `make up` just *hangs* with no error at all. `up` now plans the absent set itself (`platform/scripts/plan-implicit-builds.py`), builds it through the same guard, and passes `--no-build` so any remaining hole fails loudly instead of fanning out. `make dev` deliberately keeps compose's implicit build: its MFE layer is host-side vite servers, not containers, so only service images can be built there. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_build_guarded.py platform/scripts/test_plan_implicit_builds.py -q`.
- **AI backend mode (unified across verticals, `omnicore_svc_runtime.ai`)**: real inference-server litellm/vLLM (over Tailscale) is now the default for `make up`/`make dev` — `AI_DEV_MODE` is unset/false in `.env.example`. `AI_TEST_MODE=true` → StubLLM (deterministic, wins over `AI_DEV_MODE`). `AI_DEV_MODE=true` → local Ollama backend (`platform/compose/ollama.yml`, litellm alias `ollama-dev`). Old per-service flags (`STUDIO_AI_DEV_MODE`, `RANGE_AI_DEV_MODE`, `DIALOGUE_AI_DRAFT_DEV_MODE`) are gone — hard cutover. Per-vertical model pins (`RANGE_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `qwen3.5:9b`; `STUDIO_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss:20b`; `LITELLM_DRAFT_MODEL` for dialogue, default `gpt-oss:20b`) live as env-overridable defaults in `range-svc.yml`/`range-svc-worker.yml`/`studio-svc.yml`/`studio-svc-worker.yml`/`dialogue-svc.yml`/`dialogue-svc-worker.yml`.

- **EVERY locally-built image is tagged per stack, not just shell-mfe**: a walled stack runs `omnicore-platform/<svc>:<tag>-<name>` (e.g. `range-svc:dev-review`, and `:dev-hotreload-review` under `make dev`); shell-mfe keeps its own `:walled-<name>`. Before this, the compose project, hostname, port, mTLS tree and litellm keys were all per-stack but the ~67 `image: ...:dev` tags were machine-global, so ANY worktree's `make up STACK=<x> BUILD=...` replaced the image a different, still-running stack would resolve on its next container recreate — that stack then silently served another branch's code, and all 11 isolation vectors still passed because every one of them tested *runtime* isolation. `up`/`dev` now snapshot the tags via `docker tag` (metadata only, no rebuild) just before `up -d`; see `platform/scripts/stack-pin-images.py`.
- **A pinned stack does NOT pick up a newer `:dev` on restart — that's the point**: the snapshot is sticky, so a plain `make up STACK=<name>` keeps serving the image IDs it was pinned to even after another worktree rebuilds `:dev`. To deliberately adopt the current build, pass `REPIN=1` (`make up STACK=<name> REPIN=1`). A `BUILD=` run always builds straight into the per-stack tag, so it needs no `REPIN`.
- **Vector 12 is image provenance**: it fails a stack whose containers sit on a machine-global (unsuffixed) tag, and separately flags a container whose running image ID no longer matches what its own tag resolves to — i.e. the tag was rebuilt underneath a live container. The unwalled `platform` stack is SKIPPED there, since it legitimately owns the bare `:dev` tags.
- **Bring up infra only (for running services/tests by hand)**: `make infra`
- **Check infra health**: `make infra-test`
- **Tear the stack down**: `make down` / `make clean` (clean deletes volumes)
- **Validate a compose file**: `docker compose --env-file .env -f platform/compose/infra.yml -f platform/compose/infra.dev.yml -f platform/compose/<svc>.yml config > /dev/null`
- **One-time init + per-restart unseal for server-mode Vault**: `make vault-init` (no-op against dev-mode Vault; run after every restart of a non-dev Vault, including `infra-prod`)
- **Provision mTLS PKI locally**: `make vault-pki-bootstrap`
- **Run a service's migrations**: `make <svc>-migrate` — each service owns its own `goose_db_version_<svc>` ledger; never invoke bare `goose up`, which writes to the default `public.goose_db_version` and gets replayed on next boot
- **Lint a migration (RLS/FORCE/tenant-policy/rename-aware/audit-redaction/ledger)**: `make migration-lint`
- **Verify the audit hash chain**: `make audit-verify-identity` / `make audit-verify-org` (via `platform/cmd/audit-chain-verify --dsn --schema`; set `VAULT_ADDR`+`VAULT_TOKEN` to also check the chain against its Vault-anchored head, catching a wipe/truncation the bare walk can't see — optional, off by default)

- **Fetch + verify a Pact contract**: `make pact-verify SVC=<svc>`
- **Full local Pact round-trip**: `make pact-smoke` (needs `make infra` running)
- **Run a single Cypress spec**: `cd frontends/cypress && pnpm cypress run --spec "cypress/e2e/<v>/<journey>.cy.ts"`

All four matter: the suite talks to the BFFs directly as well as through the browser, and their `localhost:8082`/`8084` defaults are the UNWALLED primary's published ports, which a walled stack does not publish — so a `STACK=` run used to die in the first `before` hook on `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8082`, or health-check and mint personas against the primary whenever it happened to be up. Cypress also needs `experimentalSkipDomainInjection: ["*.localhost"]` (already in `cypress.config.ts`) or `cy.origin()` refuses the Keycloak hop: on a walled stack the app and `auth.` subdomain share one superdomain origin, so login fails in every spec's before-each. `cypress.config.ts` defaults `baseUrl` to `http://localhost:5173`, the UNWALLED primary, and nothing used to derive the override from `STACK=`, so the easiest way to run the suite was always against the shared stack. That is the worst default for this workload specifically: the specs MUTATE seeded data, so a full run reshapes org/user state under any other session on that stack.
- **A per-vertical BFF origin missing from `cypress-run` ERRORS the specs, it does not skip them**: `cy.request` rejects on a *connection* failure regardless of `failOnStatusCode`, so a vertical's `require<V>Up()` gate dies with `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:<port>` inside its `before all` hook and takes every spec in the file with it (studio's :8089 did exactly this — 0 of 4 tests executed until `STUDIO_BFF_URL` was set, then 4/4). The flip side is that pointing these at the stack origin makes those gates VACUOUS: `<origin>/healthz` hits shell-mfe's SPA fallback, which answers 200 with HTML, so the gate can no longer detect an absent vertical. An honest gate must probe an `/api/v1/<vertical>/` path and require a JSON content-type.

- **Run the k6 load-test harness**: `make load-test` (`SUITE=<name>`, default `smoke`; requires a running stack)
- **EVERY gate locally, in dependency order (~1h)**: `make full-local-pass` — the union of `pr-preflight`, the gates it doesn't mirror (actionlint, markdownlint, gitleaks, drift guard, files-query-lint, make-flags, cve-report, compose-isolation), CI's multi-module Go coverage MERGE gate, a real image build, a pact round-trip, and every Cypress spec against ONE stack boot. Since PR CI now runs only the cheap class, this is what gives you the signal `develop` would have. Skip stages with `SKIP=preflight,static,coverage,stack,pact,e2e`; `BUILD=none` reuses images (then it is not a build proof); `CLEAN=1` wipes volumes, which is the only way to get idempotent Cypress runs. - **Fast pre-PR gate (no Docker) — mirrors CI at changed scope**: `make pr-preflight` — runs CI's unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands for the files you changed (via `ci-changed-scope.py`), so a green run predicts green CI for those gates without spending Actions minutes. `INT=1` adds testcontainer integration. Missing local toolchains are skipped-with-hint and listed (CI still owns them).
- **Advisory full-stack Cypress dress rehearsal for one vertical**: `make pr-preflight-e2e SCOPE=<vertical>` (needs Node 20 + Chrome + Docker). - **Pre-push hook (automatic)**: `.husky/pre-push` runs a fast changed-scope smoke (Go `-short`, MFE typecheck/lint/vitest, Python `ruff`) before every push. Bypass once with `git push --no-verify` or `SKIP_PREPUSH=1`; CI still gates.
- **Read a pre-push failure you scrolled past**: the run is logged to `"$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)"/pre-push.log`, per-worktree, replaced each run; per-lane output sits in the sibling `pre-push-lanes/`. A failing run also replays each failing lane's tail after the `FAILED:` roster, so nothing is lost to scrollback. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_prepush_hook.py -q`.
- **Start a GitHub issue in its own worktree**: `./scripts/github/create-issue-branch.sh <issue> --worktree --type <type> <section>/<summary>` — creates the branch under `.worktrees/<branch>` via `make worktree` (so `.husky/_` is generated and hooks are live) and leaves the calling tree on its current branch. The epic branch is resolved to a ref, never checked out — a branch checked out in one worktree can't be checked out in another. Tests: `python3 -m pytest scripts/github/test_create_issue_branch.py -q`.
- **See every build/test/stack target**: `make help`

## CI runs on the promotion to `develop`, not on the PR

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,
the promotion of `main`: Go `-race` + coverage gate, frontend unit + coverage,
Python *integration* (testcontainers), migration lint, i18n, pact, proto
compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on
`ubuntu-24-arm-2core` and the `changes` job scopes both matrices to the services
a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

The cheap class still runs on the PR, again on the merge commit to `main`, and
again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a
GitHub-hosted ARM64 larger runner: billed, but at the ARM rate, out of its own
concurrency pool rather than the plan's 60 standard slots, and seconds-to-a-few-
minutes per job. So `main` keeps per-merge signal for these:

| Check | Workflow | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lint, Compose config validation, Keycloak realm-export lint, Branch-protection doc sync, Load-harness lib tests | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Secret Scan (gitleaks) | `secret-scan.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Action Lint | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Go Vuln Scan (govulncheck) | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| golangci-lint (new-issues-only) | `go-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, **PR only** |
| py lint / lint + typecheck + unit (`<svc>`), lint + typecheck (shared python libs) | `python-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (scoped to changed services; `integration (<svc>)` stays develop-only) |
| No duplicate Prometheus metrics in a boot graph | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image | `sign-and-verify.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (that workflow has no `main` trigger) |
| go test -short (every changed module) | `go-test.yml` | self-hosted, **push to `main` only** |

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

Consequences worth internalizing:

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

## Testing policy — Cypress e2e

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch. Any PR that adds or changes a user-facing surface owes a spec under `frontends/cypress/cypress/e2e/<vertical>/`, landed in the same branch — as does any change to login, session, invite, or org-role gating, UI diff or not. Backend-only PRs (proto, migration, service handler, BFF route with no UI consumer) don't.

Ownership is split by file, not by team:

- **Feature dev owns:** the spec files themselves, and `support/selectors.ts`.
- **QA/QC-stewarded:** the shared foundation — `cypress.config.ts`, `support/{e2e,commands,personas}.ts`, `tasks/**`, `fixtures/personas.json`.

Two things that bite:

- A spec absent from a workflow's `--spec` list did not run. Wiring it into the relevant GitHub workflow is part of authoring the spec — check that the workflow actually seeds the state the spec needs.
- `e2e.yml` is non-required and posts no check, so a green PR is not evidence a spec ran. Verify locally against `make up`.

# Frontend design system guardrails

- Per `tdd-react` on `tailwind.preset.ts` as the source of truth for `cog-*`: an
  undefined token emits no CSS and is silently invisible, not an error. This branch
  found 52 phantom tokens across 233 occurrences, including 3 passing tests that
  asserted classes rendering nothing. Grep the preset before using any `cog-*` class
  — a test asserting an undefined class is not a safety net.
- **Never inline raw hex or arbitrary Tailwind values** (`text-[#fff]`,
  `border-[1.5px]`) at a call site — define a token in the preset instead.
- **Bare numeric spacing/size utilities are banned** (`p-4`, `gap-6`, `min-h-11`) in
  favor of named `cog-*` rungs. For hit targets specifically, use `min-h-tap` /
  `min-w-tap` (44px) — never `min-h-11`.
- **WCAG 2.5.8 hit areas:** don't enlarge the visible box to hit 44×44. Move the
  drawn box into an inner `aria-hidden` span at its original size, and put the tap
  rungs on the interactive element wrapping it. Applied 7x this branch — follow the
  established pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- **Any new axis added to `tailwind.preset.ts`'s `theme.extend` must be registered in
  `frontends/ui/src/lib/cn.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge` config.** An unregistered axis
  makes `tailwind-merge` silently DELETE one of two conflicting classes — 5 live
  defects found this branch from exactly this (`text-heading-md`, `bg-cog-ai`,
  `shadow-cog-e1`, `border-field`, letterSpacing). The `CN_axis_parity` rule in
  `platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs` gates it.
- **`Design parity` (`platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs --ci`) is PR-blocking.**
  Its counts are ratchets — they may only go down, never up. A matcher change
  requires re-running with `--update` in the same PR, so the rule diff and the count
  diff review together.
- Test process for any change here: see the `tdd-react` skill.

## CI runs on the promotion to `develop`, not on the PR

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,
the promotion of `main`: Go `-race` + coverage gate, frontend unit + coverage,
Python *integration* (testcontainers), migration lint, i18n, pact, proto
compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on
`ubuntu-24-arm-2core` and the `changes` job scopes both matrices to the services
a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

The cheap class still runs on the PR, again on the merge commit to `main`, and
again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a
GitHub-hosted ARM64 larger runner: billed, but at the ARM rate, out of its own
concurrency pool rather than the plan's 60 standard slots, and seconds-to-a-few-
minutes per job. So `main` keeps per-merge signal for these:

| Check | Workflow | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lint, Compose config validation, Keycloak realm-export lint, Branch-protection doc sync, Load-harness lib tests | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Secret Scan (gitleaks) | `secret-scan.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Action Lint | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Go Vuln Scan (govulncheck) | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| golangci-lint (new-issues-only) | `go-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, **PR only** |
| py lint / lint + typecheck + unit (`<svc>`), lint + typecheck (shared python libs) | `python-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (scoped to changed services; `integration (<svc>)` stays develop-only) |
| No duplicate Prometheus metrics in a boot graph | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image | `sign-and-verify.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (that workflow has no `main` trigger) |
| go test -short (every changed module) | `go-test.yml` | self-hosted, **push to `main` only** |

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

Consequences worth internalizing:

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

## Testing policy — Cypress e2e

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch. Any PR that adds or changes a user-facing surface owes a spec under `frontends/cypress/cypress/e2e/<vertical>/`, landed in the same branch — as does any change to login, session, invite, or org-role gating, UI diff or not. Backend-only PRs (proto, migration, service handler, BFF route with no UI consumer) don't.

Ownership is split by file, not by team:

- **Feature dev owns:** the spec files themselves, and `support/selectors.ts`.
- **QA/QC-stewarded:** the shared foundation — `cypress.config.ts`, `support/{e2e,commands,personas}.ts`, `tasks/**`, `fixtures/personas.json`.

Two things that bite:

- A spec absent from a workflow's `--spec` list did not run. Wiring it into the relevant GitHub workflow is part of authoring the spec — check that the workflow actually seeds the state the spec needs.
- `e2e.yml` is non-required and posts no check, so a green PR is not evidence a spec ran. Verify locally against `make up`.
